beats.care: The Amazon stores huge amounts of carbon that shapes global weather, including the rains India depends on. Policies can actually work.
beats.what: Official satellite data shows the Brazilian Amazon lost 3,335 square kilometres between August 2025 and July 2026, the lowest since 1988.
beats.why: President Lula's government revived an anti-deforestation plan, restored fines spotted by satellite, and tied funding to cutting forest loss.

cards.body: Under the previous president Jair Bolsonaro (2019 to 2022), deforestation rose about 60%. His son Flávio Bolsonaro now faces Lula in the runoff, after taking 47% to Lula's 45% in round one. Both promise to end deforestation by 2030 or earlier.
Not yet. Fires, logging and drought now damage about 40% of the forest, often more than clear-cutting does. Fires have tripled since the election's first round.
cards.title: is the amazon safe now?

cards.body: Even at its record low, the forest lost an area over twice the size of Delhi in one year.

cards.q: Should rich countries pay to protect forests?

opts: Stricter enforcement and money tied to results
cards.q: What drove the Amazon's record-low forest loss?
cards.why: Satellite-backed fines and funding linked to cutting forest loss changed behaviour on the ground.

hook: The Amazon just had its *best year since 1988*. Will it last?

learn.t: Deforestation and land-use change are Brazil's biggest source of greenhouse gases, more than its cars or factories.

sources.title: Brazil says Amazon deforestation fell to the lowest level since 1988

sources.title: Amazon deforestation falls to lowest level since 1988, Brazil says

tldr: Brazil says Amazon forest loss fell to 3,335 sq km in the year to July 2026, the lowest since records began in 1988, days before a tight presidential runoff.
watch: Brazil votes in the presidential runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro on 25 Oct.
